english.notes:
(i) This offence is committed when a person deliberately and by some active obstruction or hindrance, aids assists in preventing a member of the railway staff from carrying out their duty, or makes it more difficult for them to do their job.
(ii) Obstruct and impede mean the same thing. Actions of a physical nature, which may also amount to an assault, against railway employees certainly fall within this offence. Verbal threats or incitements which make it more difficult for the employee to carry out a duty can likewise be treated as obstructions, however it is doubtful if mere abuse of staff would fall within section 16.
(iii) The obstruction must be wilful, and an act is done wilfully if it is deliberate and intentional rather than accidental or inadvertent. (R v Senior (1899) 1QB 283).
(iv) An employee must be doing something which is part of his/her duty as a railway employee and connected with the running of the railway, it follows that doing something unauthorised is therefore not protected by this section.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant

In Scotland: Common Law powers apply.
other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding level one on the standard scale or one month imprisonment in default of payment. (Level three or one month imprisonment in default of payment in relation to railways covered by the following: section 43 of the Channel Tunnel Act 1987; section 50 of the Midland Metro Act 1989 and section 63 of the Leeds Super tram Act 1993).

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
